name: Digital fault-tolerant STAR route puts the alpha=4 static stress-tensor force inside a ~megaquop neutral-atom budget, bypassing the hologron-decay killer that shelved HYP-017
claim: HYP-2026-017 (analog Aquila blockade-MERA force) was SHELVED on five killer issues, the decisive one (R1) being that the hologron quasiparticle decays (tau ~ ns-to-tens-of-ns) far inside the analog measurement window, so the holographic force is measured after the signal is gone. PAPER (arXiv:2606.25011, Ismail-Kornjaca-Hu-Maskara-Wang-Zhou-Zhao, 'Fast and Parallel High-Rate STAR Architecture for Megaquop Quantum Simulation') reports a concrete DIGITAL fault-tolerant budget -- ~2,240 physical qubits, ~200 s/shot, ~5.5x space reduction vs a surface-code STAR baseline -- for the EXACT 8x8 TFIM the project uses (matching the program's N=16-24 boundary-chain regime as a sub-lattice). Because it is DIGITAL fault-tolerant (gate-based logical evolution, error-corrected), it is NOT subject to the analog R1 hologron-decay obstruction: the static ground state is prepared (e.g. by adiabatic or variational logical-circuit state-prep) and the stress-tensor two-point / energy-difference force observable is measured on a fault-tolerant register with no quasiparticle-lifetime budget. HYPOTHESIS: the project's flagship STATIC observable -- the alpha=4 stress-tensor force on a critical Ising (and tricritical-Ising, HYP-027) MERA boundary chain at N=16, the SAME observable validated locally in SIM-2026-015d/051/052 -- fits inside a single-digit-megaquop STAR logical-volume budget comparable to (within ~2x of) the 2606.25011 8x8 TFIM dynamics budget, making digital FT the first credible HARDWARE route to a noise-free force detection that the shelved analog route could not deliver. This is a RESOURCE-ESTIMATION hypothesis with a hard, falsifiable budget ceiling, NOT a re-run of any analog claim.
catalogue_update_2026-06-26: RESOLVED catalogue debt: the companion paper arXiv:2509.18294 ('Transversal architecture for megaquop-scale quantum simulation with neutral atoms', Ismail et al., Sep 2025 rev May 2026) is now catalogued as PAPER-2026-127. It is the PREDECESSOR to 2606.25011/PAPER-120: transversal STAR needs ~10,000 physical qubits at 1e-3 error for FT local-Hamiltonian simulation; the high-rate STAR follow-up's ~2,240-qubit 8x8-TFIM figure is the ~5.5x improvement over this baseline. Both are now on disk and available as primary-source inputs to the resource estimate. The 'uncatalogued companion' caveat in the fields below is now cleared; costing BOTH STAR variants (transversal ~10k vs high-rate ~2.24k) bounds the gate-model uncertainty.
confidence_rationale: Low. (1) The qualitative argument is sound: a digital FT register sidesteps R1 (no quasiparticle lifetime constrains a fault-tolerant logical measurement), and 2606.25011 proves the 8x8 TFIM is inside a stated megaquop budget on neutral atoms -- so SOME holographic-Ising computation is FT-reachable. (2) Held at LOW, not medium, because the project's observable is NOT the 2606.25011 dynamics target: the paper budgets TIME-EVOLUTION to T*, whereas the force needs (a) GROUND-STATE preparation of a CRITICAL chain (state-prep cost not in the paper's dynamics budget and potentially dominant -- critical-state prep is hard) and (b) a MERA-structured boundary state or a logical two-point-correlator measurement whose logical-volume cost is unestimated. (3) The companion 'transversal STAR' paper arXiv:2509.18294 is flagged UNCATALOGUED and may change the gate-count assumptions. (4) This is a feasibility ESTIMATE; until the state-prep + correlator logical volume is actually costed against the STAR distillation/footprint model, the budget comparison is a conjecture. The hypothesis is worth recording because it is the FIRST hardware route that clears R1, but its confidence cannot exceed low before the estimate is done.
test_design: RESOURCE ESTIMATION (no quantum hardware run; a costing computation against the 2606.25011 STAR model). Steps: (1) CATALOGUE the two papers first: 2606.25011 (main) and the flagged companion 2509.18294 (transversal STAR) -- the gate model and distillation footprint must come from primary sources, not memory. (2) FIX THE TARGET CIRCUIT: the SIM-2026-015d/051/052 force observable at N=16 = (a) prepare the critical/tricritical Ising boundary ground state, (b) measure the energy-difference force V=E_dual-E_gs-dE_single OR the boundary two-point correlator across dr=1..6. Translate (a)+(b) into a logical-qubit count, logical depth, and non-Clifford (T/Toffoli) count -- the critical-state prep depth is the dominant unknown and must be estimated both for adiabatic and for a fixed-depth MERA/QAOA-style ansatz. (3) APPLY the 2606.25011 STAR footprint model (physical-per-logical at the paper's code distance, distillation factory cost, ~200 s/shot rate) to convert the logical budget into physical qubits + wall-clock + shots-for-5-sigma (reuse the SIM-2026-019 noise/SNR model: SNR=44 at dr=1, SNR=10 at dr=2 -> shots for >=5 sigma at dr=1..6). (4) COMPARE the resulting physical-qubit count and logical volume to the paper's 8x8 TFIM datapoint (2,240 physical qubits; its megaquop logical volume). (5) Report a single number: physical qubits and logical volume for the static force at N=16, with the critical-state-prep cost broken out separately (it is the swing factor). (6) Cross-check against HYP-016's analog FT atom estimates (1839 atoms / 8 min FT MERA) to state explicitly which route is cheaper for the SAME force observable.
refutation_criteria: The hypothesis ('static force fits a single-digit-megaquop STAR budget within ~2x of the 8x8 TFIM datapoint') is REFUTED if the honest resource estimate yields ANY of: (a) total logical volume for state-prep + force-correlator measurement exceeds the 2606.25011 8x8 TFIM logical volume by MORE than ~10x (i.e. not 'comparable within 2x' -- the critical-state-prep cost dominates and blows the budget); (b) physical-qubit count for >=5-sigma force detection at dr=1..6 (including shots/factory overhead at the SIM-2026-019 SNR) exceeds ~25,000 physical qubits (an order of magnitude above the paper's 2,240, i.e. no longer 'megaquop-class' for this observable); (c) the critical ground-state preparation depth on the logical register is provably super-polynomial / not bounded, so no fixed FT budget exists. The hypothesis is SUPPORTED if the static force at N=16 lands within ~2x the paper's 8x8 TFIM logical volume and under ~5,000 physical qubits including detection overhead. INCONCLUSIVE if the dominant uncertainty is the uncatalogued companion 2509.18294 gate model (resolve by costing both transversal and non-transversal STAR).
hardware_required: NONE for the test itself (this is a paper-based resource-estimation computation, local CPU only: read 2606.25011 + 2509.18294, fix the logical circuit, apply the STAR footprint model, combine with the SIM-2026-019 SNR model). NO quantum hardware run is proposed or authorized by this hypothesis -- it estimates whether a future FT run is in budget. Any actual FT hardware run would be a SEPARATE, later, explicitly-approved step (the Qiskit/hardware builders never submit without user approval per project rules).

KILLER-ISSUE RELEVANCE: this hypothesis EXISTS BECAUSE it clears HYP-017's R1 (digital FT has no quasiparticle-lifetime window); but it must NOT inherit HYP-017's R2 (the costed observable must be the validated energy-difference/two-point estimator, NOT the broken product-of-single-site-density estimator) and R3 (NO S_topo=-ln(2) target -- the force, not TEE). The estimate is cheap and falsifiable, so TESTABLE_NOW, but confidence stays LOW until the critical-state-prep logical volume (the swing factor) is actually computed.
feasibility_mandatory_gates: CATALOGUE BOTH papers first (2606.25011 main + the flagged companion 2509.18294 transversal STAR) and take the gate/footprint model from the primary sources, not memory -- the distillation/footprint assumptions drive the whole estimate.

Cost the PROJECT's validated static observable (energy-difference force V=E_dual-E_gs-dE_single or boundary two-point correlator at dr=1..6, N=16), NOT the paper's dynamics target. Break out CRITICAL-GROUND-STATE-PREP logical volume separately -- it is the dominant unknown and the swing factor for the verdict.
Combine with the SIM-2026-019 SNR model (SNR=44 @ dr=1, SNR=10 @ dr=2) to get shots-for-5-sigma and fold factory/shot overhead into the physical-qubit number; do NOT report a state-prep-only budget.
Do NOT propose, schedule, or authorize any actual FT hardware run from this hypothesis -- it is a budget estimate only; an FT run is a separate, later, explicitly-approved decision.
philosophical_implications: [SPECULATIVE, interpretive_confidence=low] HYP-017's shelving meant the emergent holographic force was confirmed only in classical numerics, never on hardware -- leaving the 'simulator realism' question (does the emergent geometry have intervention-based empirical standing, or is it only an interpretation of classical tensor-network data?) unanswered for this observable. A digital FT route that fits a megaquop budget would, for the first time, make the alpha=4 stress-tensor force a noise-free, error-corrected, hardware-falsifiable measurement -- converting a numerical regularity into a manipulability-grade empirical claim on a physical quantum computer, the same epistemic upgrade HYP-027's hardware-toggle aspiration sought but via a digital rather than analog path. The estimate itself, even before any run, has modest epistemic value: it tells us whether the program's flagship result is hardware-reachable IN PRINCIPLE within the current FT roadmap, or whether it remains a numerics-only claim for the foreseeable future -- a concrete answer to 'how far is this from being physics rather than computation.' Standard caveat: a confirmed budget is a necessary, not sufficient, condition for that epistemic upgrade; the run would still measure boundary-CFT stress-tensor structure, with the bulk geometry remaining an interpretation OF that data. Frameworks: simulator realism, manipulability/interventionist accounts of empirical content, the numerics-vs-experiment threshold.

justified_by_note: Added 2026-08-17 per audit D-10. SIM-2026-054's own verdict string is 'SUPPORTED (conditional; confidence LOW)', which this status mirrors. Dependency flagged 2026-08-17: this is a resource-estimate hypothesis for fitting a STATIC alpha = 4 force into a fault-tolerant qubit budget, and alpha = 4 is withdrawn by SIM-2026-072 (corrected: 2.6 +/- 0.2, channel OPEN). The gate-count arithmetic is unaffected -- it depends on the MERA preparation depth, not on the exponent -- but the SHOT budget does not: the number of separations and the statistical precision needed to resolve a 2.6 exponent against a 2.0 alternative is a different, and tighter, requirement than resolving 4 against 2. The estimate should be re-costed against the corrected target before it is quoted.
result_note_2026-06-26: TESTED via resource estimate (SIM-2026-054), verdict SUPPORTED-conditional, confidence stays LOW. The N=16 static alpha=4 force fits a single-digit-megaquop neutral-atom STAR FT budget: ~3,700-4,550 physical qubits on the high-rate STAR (the SOURCED 2,240 8x8-TFIM figure scaled by the logical-qubit ratio 20/12 + magic-state factory) -- under the 5k SUPPORTED ceiling -- and logical volume ~0.03x the 8x8 datapoint VIA log-depth MERA/ansatz state-prep (cross-checked against the proven ADAPT-VQE critical prep, overlap 0.9998). All three pre-registered ceilings cleared on the high-rate-STAR + MERA-prep combination (vol ~0.03x < 2x; phys ~4.5k < 5k; prep log-depth/polynomial, no super-poly REFUTE). The measurement (energy-difference force) is ~64 Clifford-measurable Pauli strings, zero non-Clifford. FT per-shot error ~1e-9 collapses the Helios 2.81% noise floor so dr=1..4 fit in ~16k shots (vs >400k on Helios). CAVEATS (why confidence stays LOW, not raised): (1) the PHYSICAL-QUBIT figure is robust/sourced, but the LOGICAL-VOLUME ratio rests on an INFERRED 8x8 reference volume (~87,600) -- PAPER-120/2606.25011 does NOT publish the T-count or logical depth; it is directionally safe only because the MERA route is ~30x under the ceiling. (2) Adiabatic prep (the alternative) reaches ~9.4x volume at the rigorous N^3 bound, borderline-REFUTE -- the verdict is conditional on log-depth prep. (3) Transversal vs high-rate STAR gate model is the pre-registered INCONCLUSIVE driver but bounded (<25k both). SWING FACTOR confirmed = critical-state-prep depth. CROSS-CHECK: analog FT-atom MERA (HYP-016, ~75-1,500 atoms) is ~3-50x CHEAPER in qubits for the SAME static force and equally R1-immune, but less mature (no isometry->qLDPC map); digital STAR is the more defensible budget. NET: the flagship alpha=4 force is hardware-reachable IN PRINCIPLE within the current FT roadmap. To harden the quantitative ratio, dig the 8x8 T-count from the 2606.25011 / 2509.18294 appendices. NO hardware run authorized.
